statement: Security organising principle: prefer 'not representable' over validated, kernel-enforced over string-checked, and declared-and-bounded over discovered at runtime; §11.2 assigns every historical vulnerability class to one of these three mechanisms.
Path traversal via '..' is not representable: LogicalPath rule P1 means no '..' component exists in the model.
research_needed: Conformance tests proving encoders/decoders reject any '..' component and that no escape via encoding variants (e.g. overlong/alternate bytes) exists.

statement: Absolute paths are not representable: rule P2 forbids a root, drive letter, or UNC prefix in a LogicalPath.
research_needed: Conformance cases for drive-relative, UNC, device-namespace (\\?\) and NT-object path forms confirming none is expressible.

statement: Separator confusion between archive and reader is not representable: P3 makes paths component sequences, so there is no separator to disagree about.
refines_or_supersedes: Narrowed by P8 row (§11.2 L1346) and §26.4 L2637/§26.5 L2679: backslash bytes remain legal in components and are handled as a detected class, not eliminated.
research_needed: Verify P3 claim does not overstate: a component containing a backslash is a target-hostile byte on Windows (P8), so the elimination holds only within the archive, not at extraction.

statement: Target-hostile bytes in a component (backslash, colon, control characters) are legal in the archive so POSIX trees archive faithfully, but are detected; the extractor must refuse or rename them on targets where they are structural (P8).
refines_or_supersedes: §26.4 L2637 narrowed the earlier claim that the model eliminates backslash traversal; §26.5 L2679 added this row.
research_needed: Enumerate per-target structural byte sets (Windows, macOS HFS+/APFS, SMB, FAT/exFAT) and test that detection is complete; usability study of the refuse-vs-rename default.
decision_needed: What is the default on a hostile component: refuse or rename, and what deterministic rename scheme is used?

statement: One name denoting both a file and a directory is not representable: P6 allows a path to be a proper prefix of another only if it is a Directory.
refines_or_supersedes: §26.5 L2679: this row was missing and added in the second review pass; §26.4 L2636 introduced P6/I26.
research_needed: Conformance corpus cases for file/dir ambiguity, including trailing-slash and case-folded variants on case-insensitive targets.

statement: Duplicate path ambiguity is not representable: P4 uniqueness invariant forbids two entries with the same path.
research_needed: Define equality for uniqueness (byte-exact components) and test decoders reject duplicates in both STREAM and INDEXED layouts.

statement: Hardlink-before-target hazards are not representable because hardlinks are modelled as content sharing, not link entries (§3.3).
Hardlink-to-symlink structural ambiguity is not representable, but only for ordering and target-resolution hazards; inode-identity fidelity is handled as metadata (§3.3a).
refines_or_supersedes: Scope limited by §3.3a (what abolishing the hardlink kind does not solve).

statement: Conflicting metadata authorities are not representable: invariants I1 and I19 require one authority and one declaration per fact.
A Directory entry carrying content is not representable (§3.3).
SFX/prefix confusion and polyglot files are not representable because no prefix is permitted before the magic (§11.4).
Trailing data after the archive is not representable because the archive declares its total length (§4.4).
research_needed: Conformance tests that readers reject files with appended bytes; clarify that 'not representable' here really means 'detected and rejected', since bytes can always be appended externally.
decision_needed: Is trailing data a hard rejection in every reader (including salvage/inspect), or reported?

statement: Multiple archive terminators are not representable (§4.4).
Parser differentials in general are 'structurally reduced, then tested' (mechanisms in §11.4), not eliminated.
research_needed: Differential testing of multiple independent Entrybound readers (reference and minimal reader) over the conformance corpus and fuzzed inputs.

statement: Symlink escape during extraction is prevented by kernel-enforced confinement (§11.6).
research_needed: Adversarial extraction tests with pre-existing and concurrently-created symlinks on each supported OS.

statement: TOCTOU races during extraction are prevented by kernel-enforced confinement (§11.6).
research_needed: Race-injection tests (concurrent rename/symlink swap) against the extractor on Linux, macOS, Windows.

statement: Windows junction escape is prevented by kernel-enforced confinement (§11.6).
research_needed: Test junctions, mount points, symlinks and other reparse tags (including cloud-file placeholders) under the NtCreateFile per-component scheme.

statement: Decompression bombs are handled by declared-and-bounded resource budgets (§11.5).
Extreme entry counts are handled by declared-and-bounded resource budgets (§11.5).
Resource exhaustion in general is handled by declared-and-bounded budgets (§11.5).
research_needed: Identify resource axes not covered by the eight budget fields (e.g. CPU time, open handles, dictionary count, Merkle depth, receipt size).

statement: Malicious sparse representations are handled as declared-and-bounded (§10.7).
refines_or_supersedes: §26.5 L2675 later simplified sparse handling to holes-as-chunks with a hole plan.

statement: Integer and size overflow are handled as declared-and-bounded via invariants I19 and I20.
research_needed: Fuzzing and checked-arithmetic audit of all size/offset computations in decoder.

statement: Unbounded header lists are prevented by I20 (every count bounded and declared).
Malicious extension metadata is handled fail-closed and authenticated (§10.3 criticality, §20.1 feature tiers).
Unsafe device nodes are policy-gated and off by default (§11.7).
setuid/setgid restoration is policy-gated and off by default (§11.7).
Windows reserved names and aliases (e.g. device names) are detected and refused by policy (P5), not eliminated by the model.
research_needed: Complete, version-aware list of Windows reserved names/aliases (CON, COM¹-style superscripts, trailing dots/spaces, 8.3 short names) and tests.

statement: Unicode normalisation and case collisions are detected and refused by policy (P5).
research_needed: Define which case-folding and normalisation tables are used (NTFS upcase table, APFS, ext4 casefold) and their versioning; measure collision detection cost.
decision_needed: Which folding/normalisation algorithm and Unicode version defines a collision, and is it per-target?

statement: Spec claims thirteen vulnerability classes are eliminated by the model, but the §11.2 table contains twelve 'Not representable' rows; the count is internally inconsistent.
refines_or_supersedes: §26.5 L2682 claims miscounts were fixed; §26.5 L2679 added rows to this table.
research_needed: Reconcile count against table; determine whether a class is missing from the table or the number is stale.
decision_needed: Is there a thirteenth eliminated class missing from the table, or should the claim say twelve?

statement: A ZIP reference extractor's traversal, symlink and absolute-path defences are opt-in flags, all disabled together by one option, and absolute paths are permitted by default.
research_needed: Primary-source check of the named extractor's options and defaults (current version).

statement: An Entrybound reader has nothing to decide about '..' or absolute paths because the archive cannot express them; the defence is removed from the implementation.
research_needed: Verify decoders never need path-sanitising code paths; formal check that the canonical encoding admits no such component.

statement: A major language's documentation states that a string-sanitising safe-extraction filter is not a confinement mechanism and that its hardened filter is insufficient for untrusted input.
research_needed: Cite the primary documentation (language, version, section).

statement: Entrybound applies both layers: the model removes vulnerability classes and the extractor additionally confines whatever remains (defence in depth rather than sanitise-then-open).
Parser-differential mechanism 1 (strongest): one authority per fact (I1, I19).
Historical parser differentials cluster overwhelmingly around fields that are declared twice.
evidence_in_source: assertion, presumably from Research I; no data in slice
research_needed: Quantified classification of historical archive CVEs/differentials by root cause.

statement: Every archive has exactly one canonical serialisation of its model; `entrybound verify --canonical` checks it.
refines_or_supersedes: §25.1 #1 L2533 defers the manifest/descriptor serialisation encoding, constrained to support this canonical form.
research_needed: Formal/fuzz proof that the chosen encoding is canonical (unique byte form per model) and that verify --canonical detects every non-canonical variant.
decision_needed: What exactly is covered by 'canonical serialisation' (manifest/descriptor only, or whole container)?

statement: §11.4 says two writers producing the same model produce the same bytes, but §12.1 makes byte-identical containers depend on planner ID, format version and writer version, unencrypted only; the scope of the same-bytes guarantee is inconsistent.
research_needed: Define precisely which byte ranges are canonical across independent writers versus writer-version dependent.
decision_needed: Does cross-writer byte identity apply to the canonical manifest serialisation only, or to whole containers?

statement: Strict parsing with no recovery or best-effort reader: an archive is conforming or rejected with a named reason code.
Recovery is a separate, explicitly labelled operation (`entrybound salvage`, §17.4) whose output is marked unverified (I25).
refines_or_supersedes: §26.4 L2655: salvage/repair were referenced normatively before being specified in §17.2.
research_needed: Define how the 'unverified' marker is carried so it cannot be dropped by downstream tools.

statement: A conformance corpus ships from v1 as a core deliverable (§19.3); it is described as the parser-differential mechanism that actually works.

The highest-impact archive vulnerabilities of the last three years were name-resolution bugs (components disagreeing whether a name is a file or directory in a fully valid archive), not memory-safety bugs.
evidence_in_source: asserted empirical basis (Research I/III); specific CVEs not cited in slice
research_needed: Cite the specific vulnerabilities and impact ranking used to support this claim.

statement: No prefix, suffix or polyglot: magic at offset 0 and the declared length ends the file; a file that is simultaneously a valid Entrybound archive and a valid executable, ZIP or tar is not a valid Entrybound archive.
research_needed: Confirm the magic/footer design makes ZIP (end-of-central-directory scan) and tar polyglots detectable, and define the detection test.
decision_needed: How does a reader detect it is inside a polyglot (e.g. ZIP EOCD appended inside declared length)?

statement: The self-extracting-archive pattern is deliberately foreclosed (§22.5).
Resource enforcement uses two independent budgets, a declared budget and a policy budget, and the archive controls neither's enforcement.
Declared budget (§4.2 item 7) has eight fields: entry count, total logical bytes, largest single entry, maximum expansion ratio, chunk count, path depth, metadata bytes, maximum key-derivation cost.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with §4.2 L380; §26.5 L2672 corrected an earlier nine-field list lacking a KDF bound.
research_needed: Validate that the eight fields bound all attacker-controllable allocation paths (dictionaries, Merkle trees, receipts, signatures, recipients).

statement: Decode window and decode working memory are declared separately as DecodeRequirements (§4.2 item 6) and enforced by the same budget algorithm.
research_needed: Measure whether declared working-set memory is computable per codec/transform (including reconstructive transforms and dictionaries).

statement: The key-derivation cost bound is enforced: an archive declaring a memory-hard KDF cost above the policy ceiling is refused before the KDF runs.
refines_or_supersedes: Strengthens §9.11 L1183 (parameters stored and reported by inspect): reporting alone is called a DoS vector; §4.2 L389 and §26.5 L2672 concur.
evidence_in_source: design rationale; comparison to one proprietary format
research_needed: Define a scalar or vector 'KDF cost' (memory, iterations, parallelism) and test pre-KDF refusal ordering.
decision_needed: How is KDF cost expressed in one budget field for Argon2id's multi-parameter cost?

statement: §9.11 biases password KDF parameters to the high-cost offline end, while §11.5 refuses archives above the caller's KDF ceiling; the default ceiling must admit strong legitimate archives yet bound DoS, and no value is given.
refines_or_supersedes: Tension with §9.11 L1184; default budget values deferred in §25.1 #16 L2548 and password KDF defaults in #12 L2544.
research_needed: Measure Argon2id time/memory on low-end target devices vs default parameters; survey guidance.
decision_needed: What default KDF-cost ceiling does the CLI policy use relative to the default archive KDF parameters?

statement: The policy budget is supplied by the caller: a default in the CLI and an explicit ExtractionPolicy in the library.
Budget algorithm step 1: read preamble; if BudgetDeclared=false, skip to step 3 and record that the archive made no declaration.
refines_or_supersedes: §26.5 L2671 added the BudgetDeclared=false branch to §11.5 (earlier text asserted unconditional declaration); I17 amended (§3.9 L329).

statement: If the declared budget or DecodeRequirements exceed the policy budget, refuse before allocating anything and report which limit was exceeded and by how much.
research_needed: Test that no allocation proportional to declared values occurs before comparison; define reason codes.

statement: During decode, reality is validated continuously against the declaration; if reality exceeds the declaration, decoding aborts and the archive is treated as hostile.
research_needed: Measure overhead of continuous accounting (e.g. running expansion ratio, metadata bytes) and define checkpoints for each field.

statement: The policy budget is independently enforced during decode so a false-but-consistent declaration still cannot exceed caller limits.

No widely used archive format declares these bounds: ZIP has no memory, entry-count or expansion bound; tar declares nothing; closest prior art declares only a decode window; one proprietary format bounds a KDF iteration count in one field.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with §4.2 L401.
research_needed: Primary-source survey of resource declarations in ZIP, tar, 7z, RAR5, zstd, xz, Apple Archive, WIM, squashfs.

statement: Default policy budgets are conservative and documented, and the CLI reports whenever it raises them.
refines_or_supersedes: Default values deferred to detailed design (§25.1 #16 L2548).
research_needed: Corpus measurement of real archive entry counts, sizes, expansion ratios, path depths to set defaults with acceptable false-refusal rate.
decision_needed: What are the default policy budget values, and when may the CLI raise them (e.g. --budget)?

statement: Concrete default resource-budget values are not specified in the security model; only the mechanism is fixed.
refines_or_supersedes: §25.1 #16 L2548 lists 'Default resource-budget values' as deferred with §11.5 mechanism fixed.
research_needed: Empirical corpus study of archive shapes and hostile-archive thresholds.
decision_needed: What default values ship for each of the eight budget fields and DecodeRequirements?

statement: Normative extraction never validates path strings then calls ordinary file operations; it resolves one component at a time against held directory descriptors using the platform containment primitive.
research_needed: Safe-Rust feasibility of descriptor-relative extraction on each OS (e.g. rustix/cap-std/windows-sys) and syscall cost per component.

statement: Linux primitive: openat2 with in-root resolution, symlink resolution disabled for interior components, and optional cross-device restriction.
research_needed: Minimum kernel version; behaviour under container seccomp profiles that block openat2 (ENOSYS/EPERM); semantics of RESOLVE_IN_ROOT vs RESOLVE_BENEATH for absolute symlinks.
decision_needed: What happens on Linux kernels or sandboxes where openat2 is unavailable?

statement: macOS primitive: openat with resolve-beneath and no-follow-any flags.
research_needed: Confirm minimum macOS version providing both O_RESOLVE_BENEATH and O_NOFOLLOW_ANY, and the fallback for older supported releases.
decision_needed: What is the minimum supported macOS version for kernel-enforced extraction?

statement: Windows primitive: relative NtCreateFile from a parent handle, one component at a time, opening reparse points rather than following them, with the root handle held without delete-sharing so it cannot be renamed away.
research_needed: Feasibility of NT native API from Rust (unsafe FFI, stability of ntdll), behaviour with ancestors of the root being renamed, OneDrive placeholders, long-path limits, and performance.
decision_needed: Is using the NT native API acceptable under the dependency/unsafe policy, or is a Win32-level equivalent required?

statement: Each of the six normative extraction patterns closes a documented race.
evidence_in_source: assertion; races not cited in slice
research_needed: Attach the documented race/CVE for each pattern to the evidence base and a regression test per pattern.

statement: Pattern 1: on the kernel's 'cannot prove containment' signal, retry a bounded number of times, then fail hard; never fall back to string validation.
research_needed: Choose retry bound; test behaviour under adversarial concurrent renames (liveness vs DoS).
decision_needed: What is the retry bound, and is it configurable?

statement: Pattern 1 forbids falling back to string validation, yet L1436 allows implementations lacking a primitive to operate in a reported weaker confinement mode; which weaker modes are permitted and whether they proceed by default is unspecified.
research_needed: Enumerate weaker-mode designs (e.g. per-component openat + O_NOFOLLOW + fstat checks) and their residual race windows per platform.
decision_needed: Which confinement modes exist, and does a weaker-than-kernel mode require explicit opt-in or just a printed warning?

statement: Pattern 2: never touch metadata by path; open each object once and use descriptor-relative operations for every metadata write (mode, owner, xattrs, timestamps).
evidence_in_source: design rule; references a documented sandboxing gap
research_needed: Per-platform availability of descriptor-based metadata APIs for ACLs, xattrs, ADS, birth time, file attributes, and resource forks.

statement: Confinement primitives cover open but not chmod/chown/setxattr/timestamp setting, and a sandboxing mechanism explicitly cannot close that gap; the only fix is never re-resolving.
evidence_in_source: reference to unnamed sandboxing mechanism documentation
research_needed: Cite the sandboxing mechanism's documentation (e.g. which LSM/sandbox) and confirm the gap.

statement: Symlink and special-file metadata: restore via a descriptor-to-path bridge where available, or decline and record the omission in the extraction fidelity report; silently setting it by path is a conformance violation.
refines_or_supersedes: §26.4 L2654: earlier extraction patterns omitted symlink metadata.
evidence_in_source: design rule; acknowledges no clean answer
research_needed: Per-platform bridge availability (Linux O_PATH/AT_EMPTY_PATH or /proc/self/fd, macOS, Windows FILE_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT) and behaviour in minimal containers without /proc.

statement: Symlink/special-file metadata restoration 'has no clean answer'; the spec does not define the 'extraction fidelity report' (distinct from the in-archive FidelityReport of §10.9) nor its schema or delivery.
research_needed: Design and usability test of an extraction-time report; relation to §10.9 FidelityReport types.
decision_needed: What is the extraction fidelity report's schema, and is it emitted by the library, the CLI, or both?

statement: Directories are created by descriptor-relative directory-create against the parent handle, then opened; the extractor never invents a directory or its mode and creates exactly what the archive declares, in canonical parent-before-child order.
refines_or_supersedes: §26.4 L2654: directory creation was previously unspecified.
research_needed: Verify canonical order (§3.4 length-prefixed component comparison) yields parent-before-child for all inputs; test with --include/--exclude subsets.

statement: Creating directories with their declared modes parent-first can block child creation when a directory is read-only or lacks write/search bits; deferred application of directory modes and timestamps is not specified.
research_needed: Test extraction of read-only directories and directory mtime preservation across platforms.
decision_needed: Are directory modes/timestamps applied after children are written, and via held descriptors?

statement: With --include/--exclude (CLI §17.3 L1864), the rule 'never invent a directory' interacts with partial extraction: whether excluded ancestor directories are still created from their declared entries is unspecified.
decision_needed: Does selective extraction always create declared ancestor directories of included entries?

statement: Pattern 3: always exclusive-create; on collision apply caller's --on-collision policy (default refuse); never unlink an existing file on own initiative (I16); for overwrite, unlink via parent descriptor and retry with bounded count; never truncate onto an existing path.
refines_or_supersedes: §26.4 L2654: earlier text hard-coded unlink-on-collision.

statement: §11.6 describes an 'overwrite' collision policy, but the unpack CLI (§17.3 L1867) offers only refuse|rename|skip; whether overwrite exists, and rename's naming scheme, are unresolved.
refines_or_supersedes: Conflicts with §17.3 L1867 --on-collision refuse|rename|skip.
decision_needed: Is 'overwrite' a supported collision policy in CLI and library, and what deterministic rename scheme is used?

statement: Pattern 4: hold the root directory handle for the entire extraction.
Pattern 5: resolve exactly one path component per call; any code path that reconstructs and re-opens a full path reintroduces the race.
research_needed: Benchmark per-component syscall overhead for deep trees and many small files on each OS (notably Windows NtCreateFile), and handle-cache strategies that preserve the guarantee.

statement: Pattern 6: never emulate a link by extracting a second copy unless that copy independently passes the same policy.
evidence_in_source: design rule; cites a language adding a distinct error
research_needed: Identify where Entrybound would emulate links (e.g. hardlink/content-sharing restore on filesystems without hardlinks) and test policy re-application.

statement: A major language added a distinct error specifically because link emulation can smuggle a member past an extraction filter.
research_needed: Cite the language, version and error.

statement: Symlinks are written as data and never traversed during extraction; their targets are not resolved, validated against the filesystem, or used to locate anything.
research_needed: Windows symlink creation privileges (SeCreateSymbolicLink / developer mode) and fallback when symlinks cannot be created.
decision_needed: What happens on Windows when the extracting user cannot create symlinks?

statement: Where a platform lacks a containment primitive the implementation must say so: a conforming extractor reports its confinement mode, `entrybound unpack` prints it when weaker than kernel-enforced, and silence is an I25 violation.
research_needed: Enumerate platforms (BSDs, illumos, WASI, older kernels, Android) and their achievable confinement mode.
decision_needed: Which platforms are supported with which confinement modes?

statement: setuid, setgid and sticky bits are not restored by default; restoration requires explicit policy.
refines_or_supersedes: CLI §17.3 L1866 --allow lists setuid but not sticky explicitly.

statement: Device nodes are not created by default; creation requires explicit policy plus privilege.
FIFOs and sockets are not created by default; creation requires explicit policy.
research_needed: Semantics of 'creating' a socket entry (bind-created socket files vs placeholders) per platform; Windows has no FIFO/socket file equivalent (AF_UNIX sockets aside).
decision_needed: What does restoring a socket entry mean, and what is recorded when a target cannot represent it?

statement: Ownership is not restored by default (files owned by the extracting user); restoration requires explicit policy plus privilege.
research_needed: Contrast with incumbent root-extraction defaults (e.g. GNU tar restores ownership as root) and assess migration surprise.

statement: Absolute-target symlinks are written as-is and never followed; no policy option applies.

Writing absolute or escaping symlink targets as-is is safe for Entrybound's own extractor but leaves traps for later tools that follow them; no policy exists to refuse or neutralise such symlinks (some incumbents' safe filters refuse them).
research_needed: Threat analysis of post-extraction symlink following by other software; survey incumbent safe-filter behaviour.
decision_needed: Should the default or a named policy refuse absolute or out-of-tree symlink targets?

statement: Windows alternate data streams are restored by default; a policy can disable it.
research_needed: Security review of restoring attacker-supplied ADS (including Zone.Identifier and streams on directories) and behaviour on non-NTFS targets (FAT/exFAT/ReFS/SMB).

statement: Zone/provenance (origin) markers are restored and propagated to extracted members by default, with a policy to disable; described as a deliberate strengthening since archivers commonly fail to propagate them.
evidence_in_source: design rationale; references a well-known failure mode
research_needed: Per-platform mechanics (Windows Zone.Identifier ADS, macOS com.apple.quarantine xattr) and test of propagation from the archive file's own marker; library vs CLI behaviour.

statement: Propagation source is unspecified: whether extracted members inherit the .eb file's own on-disk origin marker, markers stored inside the archive, or both, and how conflicts between them and library callers without a source file are handled.
decision_needed: Which marker wins when the archive file's marker and a stored member marker differ, and how does a library caller supply provenance?

statement: The well-known failure mode for origin markers is an archiver failing to propagate them to extracted files.
research_needed: Cite MOTW-bypass advisories for archivers.

statement: I16: no archive field changes what an extractor is willing to do; no restore-setuid flag, no requested extraction path, no embedded policy. The archive describes; the caller decides.
research_needed: Audit every archive-declared field (including hostility summary, archive role, zone markers, budgets) to confirm none can expand extractor behaviour.

statement: An archive may declare that it contains device nodes (hostility/class summary) so a caller can refuse early, but such declarations grant nothing.
refines_or_supersedes: Relates to preamble item 11 collision and hostility class summary (§4.2 L384).
research_needed: Verify the declaration is validated against actual entries (a lying summary must abort like a lying budget).

statement: Logical determinism: same input files and same identity profile always produce the same LAI.
research_needed: Cross-platform tests (traversal order, filesystem, locale) that LAI is invariant; independent implementation computing LAI.

statement: Planner determinism: same input, planner ID and declared resource model produce the same plan and chunk boundaries, guaranteed in deterministic mode.
research_needed: Cross-machine reproducibility tests varying cores, memory, OS, and filesystem order.
decision_needed: Outside deterministic mode, which plan properties may vary with the environment?

statement: Physical determinism: same input, planner ID, format version and writer version yield a byte-identical container, for unencrypted archives only; opt-in, and default under --deterministic.
research_needed: Reproducibility test harness across writer builds and platforms; identify residual nondeterminism (codec versions, timestamps, receipts).
decision_needed: Is physical determinism tied to exact writer version, and what counts as the same writer version?

statement: Encryption non-determinism: ciphertext of encrypted archives is intentionally never reproducible.
Frozen-planner rule: balanced-v1 produces the same plan for the same input indefinitely, a compatibility promise equal in weight to the format version.
research_needed: Golden plan test vectors per planner ID maintained in CI for the life of the planner.

statement: Planner improvements ship as new planner IDs; existing IDs are never changed, only eventually deprecated for new archives while remaining fully decodable.
Keeping planner output identical indefinitely is sustainable; it implicitly freezes third-party encoder versions whose output bytes can change across releases.
refines_or_supersedes: §26.4 L2648 acknowledges frozen planner IDs freeze third-party encoder versions; §5.7.
research_needed: Measure output drift of candidate codecs (zstd, xz, brotli) across versions at fixed parameters; estimate cost of vendoring/pinning encoders.
decision_needed: Does the frozen plan promise cover compressed bytes (requiring pinned encoders) or only plan decisions and chunk boundaries?

statement: 'Same input' for determinism excludes available memory, core count, wall-clock time, locale, filesystem traversal order and machine identity; a deterministic planner reads a declared resource model instead of the environment (§5.7).
refines_or_supersedes: §26.4 L2649 later added floating point, wall-clock budgets and iteration order to §5.7.

statement: A mainstream codec recently made multithreading its CLI default, and its multithreaded output is not bit-identical to single-threaded output at the same level; a reproducible format must own that variable.
refines_or_supersedes: Listed in §26.2 L2600 as verified 2026-08-29 against primary sources.
evidence_in_source: primary-source verification claimed in §26.2; codec not named in slice
research_needed: Record the codec, version and measurement for the evidence base.

statement: Byte-deterministic ciphertext and semantically secure encryption cannot coexist; Entrybound states this rather than pretending otherwise.
Byte-deterministic encryption requires deriving keys and nonces from plaintext (convergent encryption), inheriting confirmation-of-a-file and learn-the-remaining-information attacks (§9.7).
evidence_in_source: literature-based reasoning; no citation in slice
research_needed: Cite convergent-encryption attack literature in evidence base.

statement: Nonce-misuse-resistant AEAD modes are not a loophole: their specification states a repeated nonce discloses whether two messages are equal.
research_needed: Cite the specification section (e.g. RFC 8452 security considerations).

statement: The plaintext canonical form is byte-deterministic: canonical entry order, normalised optional fields, declared timestamps.
research_needed: Define 'normalised optional fields' and 'declared timestamps' precisely; test canonical plaintext identity under encryption.
decision_needed: What does 'declared timestamps' mean for the plaintext canonical form given timestamps are preserved metadata?

statement: The ciphertext is explicitly non-deterministic and the specification must say so.
Reproducibility is anchored to LAI, not container bytes: two independent builds yield the same LAI even though their encrypted containers differ entirely.
research_needed: Independent-build test producing identical LAI for encrypted outputs from separate machines.

statement: A signature's content_binding covers LAI and AUX (§9.6) and survives re-encryption and recompression; physical_binding and addressing_binding do not, and verify reports them as stale rather than silently passing.
refines_or_supersedes: §26.5 L2669-2670 corrected this section, which previously claimed signatures survive re-encryption.
research_needed: Confirm AUX contents (fidelity report, conversion record) are unchanged by repack/re-encryption; formal analysis of binding composition.

statement: A deterministic-ciphertext mode is not offered, because it would leak file presence to anyone holding a candidate file.
refines_or_supersedes: Departs from the product brief, whose framing would permit such a mode with a documented caveat.

statement: The users who would enable a deterministic-ciphertext mode overlap almost entirely with those who would not understand its consequence.
research_needed: User research with reproducible-build and backup users on demand for deterministic encrypted outputs and understanding of the leak.

statement: Reproducible-build archive guidance enumerates timestamp, ordering, ownership and codec-header nondeterminism but says nothing about encryption; no format reconciles both goals, making Entrybound strictly better.
research_needed: Primary-source review of reproducible-builds archive guidance and competing formats.

statement: Identity participation is fixed by the identity profile (§8.3); participating by default: paths, kinds, content digests, symlink targets, executable bit.
Preserved but non-participating by default: all timestamps, ownership, full mode bits, ACLs, xattrs, platform-specific metadata, the fidelity report and the conversion record.
The identity-participating 'executable bit' is not defined relative to full mode bits (owner/any x bit) or to sources lacking POSIX modes (Windows, ZIP from DOS/NTFS hosts).
research_needed: Survey executable-bit derivation in git, Nix, and ZIP external attributes; test cross-platform LAI stability.
decision_needed: How is the executable bit derived from mode bits and from non-POSIX sources?

statement: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH-style normalisation is unnecessary for identity because timestamps do not affect LAI, while metadata is still preserved; content-addressed stores discard metadata, so this combination is offered by nobody.
research_needed: Compare with Nix NAR, OSTree, casync/desync, OCI; note physical determinism still depends on stored timestamps.

statement: Where a build system supplies an epoch, the correct semantic is clamping (no timestamp later than the epoch), not blanket setting; the reverse is described as a recurring documented error.
research_needed: Confirm clamp semantics in reproducible-builds spec; decide how clamping interacts with §12.2's 'never read environment'.
decision_needed: Is the epoch taken from the environment or an explicit flag, and is clamping recorded as a fidelity loss?

statement: The tar-streaming versus ZIP-seeking trade-off is not intrinsic but a consequence of placing authority where it serves only one access pattern.
Authority lives in a sequence of records whose position is decided by the layout (§4.1), making streaming and random access both first-class.
Sequential creation with no seeking and unknown total size is supported by STREAM layout with records after data (§4.6).
refines_or_supersedes: Encrypted STREAM scoped out of v1 (§26.4 L2646; CLI §17.3 L1857 refuses --recipient/--password with --layout stream).
research_needed: Test pipe-to-pipe creation memory bound with stream_dedup_window.

statement: Sequential extraction is supported by both STREAM and INDEXED layouts.
research_needed: Confirm an INDEXED archive can be extracted from a non-seekable input without reading the tail index first.

statement: Random entry access uses INDEXED layout and takes two range reads.
refines_or_supersedes: §13.5 L1547 describes footer, descriptor+index, then data ranges (at least three requests from cold).
research_needed: Count cold/warm round trips for random entry access; index size for million-entry archives may exceed one read.
decision_needed: Does 'two range reads' assume the footer/index is already cached?

statement: Random chunk access uses a chunk table in both compressed and logical coordinates.
Huge files are supported: 64-bit sizes everywhere, chunked content, and no whole-file buffering.
research_needed: Test >4 GiB and >2^40 byte entries across layouts and platforms.

statement: Bounded-memory operation is provided by declared decode requirements (§4.2) and per-chunk decode.
research_needed: Measure peak memory with dedup, dictionaries, reconstructive transforms and lookback>0.

statement: Partial retrieval fetches only the chunks covering the wanted range.
research_needed: Account for lookback dependencies and reconstructive transforms that require more than the covering chunks.

statement: HTTP range-friendliness via a fixed self-locating footer so the first request is one unconditional range request.
research_needed: Test suffix-range (bytes=-N) support across common servers/CDNs/object stores.

statement: Parallel decompression via independently decodable chunks (default lookback 0).
refines_or_supersedes: §26.4 L2638 fixed lookback 0 as balanced default; §22.2 L2365 scores dense/extreme only partial.
research_needed: Measure parallel decode speedup and ratio cost at lookback 0 vs solid.

statement: Parallel bulk transfer: the same chunk table serves N-connection fetch.
Resumable reading is chunk-granular and verified per chunk.
Verified partial reads use a Merkle slice over the fetched range (§8.6).
research_needed: Proof size and verification cost per range; interaction with encrypted archives.

statement: Every format that achieves seekable compression has three properties (independent units, dual-coordinate unit index, fixed self-locating tail), and every format lacking them does not seek.
evidence_in_source: synthesis of prior formats; not enumerated
research_needed: Enumerate surveyed formats (e.g. zstd seekable, BGZF, xz index, eStargz) and verify the universal claim.

statement: Independent compression units: no shared window state across any seek or parallelisation boundary; ratio on small units is preserved via shared preloaded dictionaries, which create no serial dependency, so dictionaries are first-class (§3.6).
An index of unit offsets in both compressed and logical coordinates; minimum form is a compressed-size/logical-size pair per unit, and Entrybound's chunk table adds digests.
refines_or_supersedes: Index data structure deferred (§25.1 #18 L2550).

statement: A fixed-size, self-locating tail so the first request is unconditional (§4.4).

A single-frame stream is a serial dependency chain; a widely used codec's thread flag parallelises compression only, and the same codec family becomes parallel-decodable by emitting independent blocks plus an index.
research_needed: Cite codec documentation for thread-flag scope and the seekable/indexed variant.

statement: `entrybound inspect` reports random-access granularity: worst-case bytes decoded to read one arbitrary byte, computed from chunk sizes and group lookback (§7.5).
refines_or_supersedes: CLI §17.4 L1901 `inspect --access`.

statement: The granularity metric counts chunk sizes and lookback only; whether it accounts for dictionaries, reconstructive transforms, dedup indirection, encryption segments and remote round trips is unspecified.
research_needed: Define and validate the cost model against measured random-read latency/bytes.
decision_needed: What is the normative formula for reported random-access granularity?

statement: The example 'dense archive with lookback 4' implies a dense lookback value without measurement; the access-granularity/ratio curve for lookback is deferred to empirical work.
refines_or_supersedes: §25.3 L2572 defers the lookback access/ratio curve; §6.3 L726 says only 'larger declared lookback'.
research_needed: Measure ratio vs worst-case decode bytes across lookback values on representative corpora.
decision_needed: What max_lookback values do dense and extreme use by default?

statement: Independent compression units carry a genuine ratio cost from lost cross-boundary matching, mitigated by shared dictionaries, similarity ordering and the lookback dial.
refines_or_supersedes: §23.4 L2483 quantifies it as 'a few percent versus solid' without cited measurement.
evidence_in_source: acknowledged trade-off; no measurement in slice
research_needed: Benchmark lookback-0 + dictionaries + similarity ordering vs solid 7z/xz/zstd-long on mixed corpora.

statement: An .eb archive is readable over HTTP range requests without a specialised server: one request for the footer, one for descriptor and index, then data ranges.
research_needed: Prototype and measure request counts/latency for large indexes, encrypted archives (encrypted descriptor/index), and servers lacking range support.

statement: The container-image ecosystem converged independently on the footer-plus-index range-read pattern across three separate designs; Entrybound gets it natively.
research_needed: Cite the three designs (e.g. eStargz, SOCI, zstd:chunked/Nydus).

statement: The seek index lives inside the archive rather than in a separate artifact.
refines_or_supersedes: Driven by §26.2 L2603 finding.

statement: One container-image design placed its seek index in a sidecar artifact; replication tooling separated index from data, causing inconsistent deployments and requiring a redesigned linkage.
refines_or_supersedes: §26.2 L2603 lists as primary-source verified.
evidence_in_source: primary-source verification claimed in §26.2; design unnamed
research_needed: Record the specific design and source.

statement: When a sidecar is genuinely needed (§15.4), it is bound by digest and its absence is detectable.
research_needed: Define how absence is detected by a reader that only has the data artifact.

statement: Seeking and bulk parallel transfer are distinct optimisations; the chunk table must serve both fetching one chunk and fetching all chunks over N connections.
The same ecosystem shipped a parallel eager download mode after finding that workloads accessing everything immediately gain nothing from laziness.
refines_or_supersedes: §26.2 L2604 lists as verified.

statement: Remote fetch strategy is unspecified: default connection count, range coalescing for many small chunks, multi-range requests, retry/resume policy, and caching of footer/index.
research_needed: Latency/throughput experiments against object stores and CDNs with varying chunk sizes and connection counts.
decision_needed: What remote fetch strategy and defaults does the library/CLI implement in v1?

statement: The library does not hide capability differences: asking a STREAM-layout archive for entry N returns a distinguishable 'requires a full pass or a repack' result rather than silently performing an O(n) scan.
refines_or_supersedes: Library API surface deferred (§25.1 #21 L2553); §19.4 fixes the complexity-visibility rule.
decision_needed: What is the API shape/error variant for operations requiring a full pass?

statement: An archive with lookback greater than 0 reports its true access cost rather than presenting per-chunk reads as free.
Legacy formats are foreign encodings; importing is an interpretation; because interpretation is fallible it is explicit, policy-driven and recorded.
Import produces Observations rather than Entries directly, so legacy ambiguity never reaches the native model.
refines_or_supersedes: §26.5 L2684 lists the Legacy Observation Model's shape as not overturned by review.

statement: Observation has subject (prospective entry/field), field name (name, size, mode, mtime, content-extent, ...), value, source location (exact place in source bytes), and authority kind (which structure asserted it).
research_needed: Enumerate FieldName and AuthorityKind vocabularies per adapter and SourceLocation encoding (absolute vs structure-relative offsets, nested compressed streams).
decision_needed: What are the closed vocabularies for FieldName/AuthorityKind and the SourceLocation format?

statement: Every repeated assertion of a field by a legacy source is recorded as a separate observation with source location and authority; conflicts are represented, not resolved.
Conflicts carry a severity; without one --strict would be unusable because nearly every real ZIP carries mtime in both the DOS field and an extra field at different precisions.
refines_or_supersedes: §26.4 L2651 introduced severities to fix --strict refusing almost every real ZIP.

statement: Text says 'Three severities' but defines four classes (Omission, Refinement, Divergence, Irreconcilable); Omission was added later and the count was not propagated.
refines_or_supersedes: §26.5 L2678 added Omission as a fourth class; §26.4 L2651 still says three severities.
decision_needed: Confirm the conflict class set is exactly four and fix counts in §14.2 and §26.4.

statement: Omission severity: when source conventions leave a fact implicit (e.g. a/b present with no entry for a, which P6 requires), the importer synthesises the missing Directory with a policy-determined mode and records a Synthesis entry in the receipt; permitted under --strict, never silent.
refines_or_supersedes: Added in second review pass (§26.5 L2678).

statement: The 'policy-determined mode' for synthesised directories, their timestamps/ownership, and whether facts other than missing ancestors qualify as Omission are unspecified.
research_needed: Survey incumbent extractor behaviour for implied directories (umask-based modes) and corpus prevalence.
decision_needed: What default mode/metadata does ImportPolicy assign to synthesised directories, and is Omission limited to ancestors?

statement: Refinement severity: compatible assertions where one is strictly more precise (2-second DOS vs 1-second extended timestamp) resolve to the most precise value; recorded, never a refusal.

The compatibility predicate separating Refinement from Divergence is undefined: DOS timestamps are local time without a zone while extended timestamps are UTC, so a timezone offset may make most real ZIP mtimes Divergence and refused under --strict.
research_needed: Measure on a real ZIP corpus how often DOS and extended mtimes differ beyond precision, and define per-field compatibility rules (rounding, zone).
decision_needed: What exact rule classifies two timestamp assertions as compatible (Refinement)?

statement: Divergence severity: assertions differ but the difference is representable and policy-resolvable (e.g. two different mtimes); refused under --strict, resolved by the named runtime under --compat.
Irreconcilable severity: assertions imply different content or structure (declared size disagreeing with actual stream; a name appearing twice); always refused under --strict.

Real ZIP and tar archives routinely omit ancestor directory entries, so treating omission as Irreconcilable would make --strict reject most of the corpus that §21 Stage 1 (convert --strict --dry-run) targets.
research_needed: Measure prevalence of omitted ancestors and other conflict classes in a representative ZIP/tar corpus (PyPI, Maven, npm, GitHub releases).

statement: Synthesis is safe because an omitted ancestor has exactly one possible reading, unlike disagreeing sizes which have two.
research_needed: Formally define when an ancestor is truly omitted versus asserted elsewhere as a non-directory (e.g. 'a' later appears as file or symlink, or tar entries appear out of order) and test.
decision_needed: How is an implied ancestor classified when another entry asserts a conflicting kind for that path?

statement: Import has its own declared import_budget enforced before and during import: maximum observations, maximum observations per subject, maximum conversion-record bytes, maximum entries, maximum total logical bytes.
refines_or_supersedes: §26.4 L2652 added import_budget; default values deferred (§25.1 #23 L2555).

statement: import_budget lacks fields for decompression expansion ratio, decode memory, path depth, nesting of compressed streams, and legacy KDF cost (encrypted ZIP/7z), all attacker-controlled during import; and legacy sources rarely declare totals needed for 'before' enforcement.
research_needed: Threat-model legacy import paths (nested archives, overlapping ZIP entries, deflate bombs) and map to budget fields.
decision_needed: Should import_budget include expansion ratio, memory, depth and KDF-cost bounds?

statement: Default values for import_budget fields are not given.
refines_or_supersedes: §25.1 #23 L2555 defers import resource-budget defaults.
research_needed: Corpus-based sizing of observation counts per entry and receipt sizes.
decision_needed: What are the default import_budget values?

statement: Without an import budget, a hostile ZIP asserting one field a million times would produce an arbitrarily large ConversionRecord inside an otherwise valid .eb.
research_needed: Construct such inputs in the conformance corpus and verify budget refusal.

statement: An ImportPolicy resolves the observation set into the native model, and every conflict, choice and rule applied is written to the ConversionRecord (§16).

Research III found a ZIP in a production registry's accepted test corpus whose local and central headers declare 9 bytes while deflate inflates to 51 with a CRC collision; six implementations gave five outcomes, from nine benign bytes to all 51 including an executable payload.
refines_or_supersedes: §26.1 L2589 marks Research III results as load-bearing for §14.2.
research_needed: Keep the case and observed outcomes in the conformance corpus with versioned implementations.

statement: Worked example: each size assertion (local header, central directory, deflate stream) becomes an observation with structure-relative source location and authority, and a Conflict record lists the conflicting observation indices.
research_needed: Define the Conflict record schema (severity field, observation references) which is shown but not specified.
decision_needed: What is the normative schema of a Conflict record and its severity assignment?

statement: --strict import: any unresolved conflict is a refusal; the command exits non-zero, names the conflict, cites byte offsets of each conflicting observation, and imports nothing.
--strict is the correct default for anything to be signed, published or trusted.
refines_or_supersedes: CLI §17.5 L1939 makes --strict the default for legacy-to-eb conversion.

statement: `entrybound convert --strict --dry-run` is a ZIP and tar conformance checker that no existing tool provides, making Entrybound useful before format adoption (§21 Stage 1).
research_needed: Survey existing ZIP/tar linting/validation tools (e.g. registry validators, zipdetails, libarchive checks) and user demand.

statement: --compat=<runtime> resolves conflicts per a named legacy runtime's documented or observed behaviour; the runtime name is mandatory and there is no anonymous default.
Named compat runtimes: zip/python-zipfile, zip/java-zipfile, zip/java-zipinputstream, zip/infozip, zip/libarchive, tar/gnu, tar/bsdtar, tar/python-tarfile.
research_needed: Assess coverage gaps: 7-Zip, Windows Explorer, macOS Archive Utility, Go archive/zip, .NET, Rust zip crate, and runtimes for gzip/zstd/xz multi-member handling.
decision_needed: Which runtime models ship in v1, and are compressed-stream adapters given compat runtimes?

statement: For the worked example, --compat=zip/python-zipfile imports 9 bytes and --compat=zip/infozip imports 51; both are recorded in the receipt and yield different LAIs, which is correct as they are different content.
evidence_in_source: derived from Research III measurement (versions not stated)
research_needed: Re-verify behaviour per implementation version in the observed-outcome matrix.

statement: Maintaining versioned runtime identifiers (behavioural models of eight third-party implementations tracked adversarially and indefinitely) is the largest single work item in the product.
research_needed: Effort estimate from building the first two runtime models against the corpus.
decision_needed: Is the compat runtime set resourced for v1 or narrowed?

statement: Runtime identifiers carry versions (e.g. zip/python-zipfile@3.13), because implementations change behaviour and a receipt naming an unversioned runtime records nothing durable.
refines_or_supersedes: Supersedes the unversioned example names given earlier in §14.3 L1632; CLI §17.5 L1940 shows unversioned '--compat <runtime>'.
decision_needed: What version granularity (minor vs patch) identifies a runtime, given security backports change behaviour within minors?

statement: Compat behavioural models are derived from the conformance corpus and its observed-outcome matrix (§19.3), not from reading source code; a compat model is a table lookup into the matrix, making the work bounded and auditable.

A table lookup into a finite observed-outcome matrix cannot directly predict a runtime's behaviour on a conflict pattern absent from the corpus; handling of unmatched patterns under --compat is unspecified.
research_needed: Design the matrix keying (conflict class/features) and test generalisation to fuzzed legacy inputs against the real runtimes.
decision_needed: When a conflict pattern is not in the matrix, does --compat refuse, or apply a rule-based model?

statement: The set of --compat behavioural models is deferred (§25); only its scale is acknowledged here.
refines_or_supersedes: §25.1 #22 L2554 defers --compat behavioural models per runtime.
research_needed: Build observed-outcome matrix across the named runtimes.
decision_needed: Which runtime models are built and at what versions?

statement: --preserve import retains non-semantic legacy peculiarities: full observation set including conflicts, original byte layout of extra fields and pax records, unrecognised structures, ordering and padding; content is imported under a named --compat runtime and the unresolved observation set travels in the ConversionRecord.
research_needed: Measure ConversionRecord size under --preserve vs import_budget limits; define how --preserve requires/combines with --compat in the CLI.

statement: --preserve enables zip→eb→zip round-trips for a meaningful subset of inputs and makes .eb a legitimate forensic container (everything preserved, nothing executed, ambiguity visible).
research_needed: Define the round-trippable subset and measure byte-exact round-trip rate on a corpus.
decision_needed: Does --preserve retain raw non-chosen content readings (e.g. extra bytes of a longer stream, trailing data) needed to claim 'everything preserved'?

statement: Tier 1 adapter shipped at v1: ZIP with its full defect surface, including ZIP-based .jar, .whl, .apk, .epub and .docx.
research_needed: Scope ZIP sub-features: ZIP64, split/multi-disk, compression methods beyond deflate, traditional and AES encryption, data descriptors, prepended data (APK signing block, SFX).
decision_needed: Which ZIP compression methods, encryption schemes and multi-disk variants does the v1 adapter support?

statement: Tier 1: tar family (ustar, POSIX pax, GNU, v7, star); dialect detected and recorded; PAX override precedence is modelled as an observation conflict, not a silent rule.
research_needed: Coverage of GNU sparse formats, long-name/link records, multi-volume and incremental dumps, global pax headers.

statement: If a pax record overriding a truncated ustar name/size is a conflict, its severity is unspecified; classifying it as Divergence would make --strict refuse most pax archives with long names or large files.
research_needed: Classify pax-over-ustar cases (truncation, placeholder values) and measure prevalence.
decision_needed: What severity applies when pax extended headers override ustar fields?

statement: Tier 1: gzip, single-stream; header fields (mtime, name, OS byte, extra flags) become observations.
research_needed: Handling of multi-member (concatenated) gzip, trailing garbage, and naming of the resulting entry (FNAME vs outer filename).
decision_needed: Is multi-member gzip refused, treated as one stream, or as a conflict?

statement: Tier 1: zstd, framed and skippable-frame content; the declared window is recorded.
decision_needed: Is skippable-frame content preserved in the ConversionRecord, and how are seekable-format index frames treated?

statement: Tier 1: xz, with its block index preserved and per-block integrity carried into per-chunk digests.
research_needed: Clarify how xz check types (none/CRC32/CRC64/SHA-256) relate to Entrybound's single per-format digest algorithm.
decision_needed: What does 'carried into per-chunk digests' mean when the native digest algorithm differs from xz's check?

statement: Tier 1: bzip2 as a legacy, decode-only adapter.
Tier 2 (after v1): 7z, justified by large installed base; solid folders are said to map cleanly to chunk groups.
research_needed: Verify mapping of 7z solid folders and coder chains (BCJ2 multi-stream, AES) onto bounded-lookback chunk groups.

statement: Tier 2 (after v1): OCI image layer, as the largest tar-derived corpus and a natural Stage-1 wedge (§21).
OCI layers are called a natural Stage-1 adoption wedge but the adapter is Tier 2, shipped after v1; the timing of Stage 1 relative to v1 is inconsistent.
decision_needed: Is the OCI layer adapter needed at v1 to support the Stage-1 wedge, or is Stage 1 limited to ZIP/tar?

statement: Tier 2 (after v1): RAR5 decode-only; export is not offered because the reference decoder's licence does not permit reimplementing the compressor.
research_needed: Legal review of unRAR licence terms vs clean-room decoders (e.g. libarchive) and whether decode implementation is itself permitted.

statement: Tier 2 (after v1): Nix NAR, trivial to import, and its canonical-serialisation discipline is a useful conformance test for Entrybound's own.
Tier 3 adapters (cpio, ar, WIM, squashfs, lzip, lz4, zpaq) are demand-driven with no committed timeline or demand criterion.
research_needed: Demand evidence (corpus prevalence, user requests) for each Tier 3 format.
decision_needed: What demand signal promotes a Tier 3 adapter?

statement: No legacy peculiarity acquires a native representation.

A legacy extra field becomes a native metadata item only if it maps to a typed item in a defined namespace; data descriptors and '..' components never become native structures or paths; unmapped data lives in the ConversionRecord as preserved, queryable, structurally inert legacy data.
research_needed: Mapping table from ZIP extra fields and pax keywords to closed namespaces (§10.2a); define 'structurally inert' for export/round-trip use.

statement: Import disposition of legacy paths violating P1-P8 (absolute, '..', backslashes, non-UTF-8 names, reserved names, case collisions) is unspecified beyond not becoming native: refuse, rename, or drop, and under which severity and mode.
research_needed: Corpus prevalence of hostile/odd legacy names and incumbent handling.
decision_needed: How does each import mode treat legacy entries whose names cannot be LogicalPaths?

statement: Without this boundary, three format generations of accumulated defects would flow into the native model and Entrybound would become ZIP with a different magic number.
